name: estherkim99/cs1951a-final (Databnb project)
what_it_holds: Class project ('Databnb') compiling roughly 20 Inside Airbnb scrapes per city over a 4-year window for 10 US cities (Seattle, Nashville, San Francisco, Denver, Boston, Austin, Chicago, Los Angeles, New York) plus Zillow ZHVI (507 rows) and ZRI (466 rows) housing indices, stored in SQLite; totals ~347,440 listing rows across cities. NYC and LA full CSVs were too large to commit to GitHub (attempted, then dropped); a data/database_sample.txt sample file is included. Project site: https://cs1951a-s20-brown.github.io/projects/project_data/Databnb/data.html.
why_useful: A pre-built multi-year (4-year), multi-city (10 US cities) longitudinal listing panel already joined to housing-value indices (Zillow ZHVI/ZRI) — useful as a ready cross-check dataset for STR-vs-long-term-rental crossover (gap #13) even though the underlying source is Inside Airbnb we already hold in other vintages.
geography: Seattle, Nashville, San Francisco, Denver, Boston, Austin, Chicago, Los Angeles, New York
time_coverage: ~4 years, ~20 scrapes/city (exact years not stated in visible content)
size_hint: ~347,440 listing rows (SQLite + partial CSVs; NYC/LA CSVs excluded from repo for size)
duplicate_of_holding: Underlying source is Inside Airbnb, which we already hold for a different city/vintage mix; this fills specific vintages/cities (Denver, Nashville pre-existing years) we may not have and pre-joins to Zillow housing indices

name: Airbnb Prices in European Cities (Kaggle mirror)
what_it_holds: Kaggle-hosted mirror of the academic Gyodi & Nawaro (2021, 'Determinants of price in the sharing economy: An analysis of Airbnb data') scrape: per-city weekday/weekend CSVs for roughly 10 European cities including Amsterdam, Athens, Berlin, Lisbon and Vienna from our target list (plus Barcelona, Budapest, London, Paris, Rome), collected Aug 2018 and Jan 2019, with columns for price (realSum), room_type, person_capacity, host_is_superhost, distance to city centre/metro, cleanliness/satisfaction ratings, and weekday/weekend flag. Original source is an academic Mendeley Data deposit (exact DOI/ID not independently verified this session -- a direct Mendeley URL guess 404'd, so only the Kaggle mirror is confirmed reachable).
why_useful: One of the only multi-city academic-grade Airbnb price panels that actually covers five of our ten target cities (Amsterdam, Athens, Berlin, Lisbon, Vienna) simultaneously with a consistent methodology and hedonic covariates -- useful as an older, independent cross-check on relative ADR/price levels across those markets even though it predates our current window (2018-19 vintage, one-time weekday/weekend cut, not a time series).
geography: Amsterdam, Athens, Barcelona, Berlin, Budapest, Lisbon, London, Paris, Rome, Vienna
time_coverage: Two snapshots: August 2018 and January 2019 (weekday/weekend each)
size_hint: ~51,000 listing-rows across the 10 cities per public description
license: Kaggle dataset licence not independently confirmed this session
last_activity: Underlying academic collection 2018-2019; Kaggle mirror upload date not confirmed
duplicate_of_holding: Distinct vintage/methodology from our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel and our 123-market reviews-based stays index; not previously catalogued

name: medellin-airbnb-displacement-risk
what_it_holds: Pipeline flagging Medellin/Barranquilla, Colombia neighborhoods where Airbnb growth concentrates in low-income areas. Committed: comuna_estrato.csv (Medellin socioeconomic strata by comuna), barranquilla_barrio_estrato.csv (parcel-level ESTRATO_1994 layer, maintained through 2025), dane_housing_blocks.geojson (DANE 2018 census block housing counts), medellin_barrio_housing.csv / barranquilla_barrio_housing.csv (aggregated housing units), plus geospatial boundaries: 265 barrios/16 comunas (Medellin, from GeoMedellin) and 189 barrios/5 localidades (Barranquilla, from Secretaria Distrital de Planeacion). Airbnb listings themselves are pulled via an Apify scraper (method, not a static committed dump) rather than stored point-in-time snapshots. README gives no row counts. Repo created/updated 13 Sep 2026 (one day before this scan) — very new, single contributor, unclear maturity.
why_useful: First concrete LatAm-city STR + regulation/displacement-adjacent dataset found for this theme: ties Colombian Airbnb growth to DANE census and municipal socioeconomic-strata (estrato) data for two cities not in our current Inside Airbnb panel, relevant to gap #12 (regulation/registration context) and gap #7 (regional supply/housing crossover) even though it is not a pure ADR/occupancy series.
time_coverage: DANE census baseline 2018; estrato layer maintained through 2025; Airbnb pull is live/current via Apify, not vintaged
size_hint: Several CSVs + one geojson, city-block/barrio granularity (265 + 189 areal units); no listing-level row count given
themes: Latin America STR datasets: Mexico City, Cancun, Rio, Sao Paulo, Buenos Aires, Bogota, Medellin, Lima, Santiago Airbnb data and regulation
why_all: First concrete LatAm-city STR + regulation/displacement-adjacent dataset found for this theme: ties Colombian Airbnb growth to DANE census and municipal socioeconomic-strata (estrato) data for two cities not in our current Inside Airbnb panel, relevant to gap #12 (regulation/registration context) and gap #7 (regional supply/housing crossover) even though it is not a pure ADR/occupancy series.
